questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: Amit said, "I am hungry." → Amit said that ____.
option_feedback: *I* refers to Amit, so it becomes *he*.
*had hungry* is not a correct form.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: She said, "I am writing a letter." → She said that she ____ a letter.
option_feedback: That changes the meaning to a finished action.
The continuous aspect must be kept: *was writing*.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: He said, "I have finished my work." → He said that he ____ his work.
option_feedback: The backshift of *have finished* is *had finished*.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: Ravi said, "I met her yesterday." → Ravi said that he ____ her ____.
questions.explanation: Simple past → past perfect; *yesterday → the day before*.
option_feedback: Simple past → past perfect, and *yesterday → the day before*.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: The girl said, "I can dance." → The girl said that she ____ dance.
Choose the correct reported form: He said, "I may be late." → He said that he ____ be late.
Choose the correct reported form: Father says, "I am proud of you." → Father says that he ____ proud of me.
questions.explanation: Present reporting verb → no tense change.
option_feedback: No backshift after a present reporting verb.
*he* takes *is/was*, and there is no backshift.
The reporting verb *says* is present, so the tense does not change.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: The teacher said, "Honesty is the best policy." → The teacher said that honesty ____ the best policy.
option_feedback: There is no future idea here.
A proverb or universal truth keeps the present.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: She said, "I was reading when you called." → She said that she ____ when I had called.
option_feedback: Past continuous → past perfect continuous in strict reported speech.
The continuous meaning must be kept.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: He said, "I will leave this place now." → He said that he would leave ____ place ____.
Choose the correct reported form: Mohan said to me, "You should work hard." → Mohan told me that I ____ work hard.
questions.explanation: *should, would, could, might* do not change.
option_feedback: *should* does not change in reported speech.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: Rina said to me, "I like your dress." → Rina ____.
options: told me that she liked my dress
said me that she liked my dress
told me that I liked your dress
told that she liked my dress
questions.explanation: *said to me → told me*; pronouns follow the speaker and listener.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: "We are going to Goa next week," said the boys. → The boys said that they ____ to Goa ____.
questions.explanation: *are going → were going*; *next week → the following week*.
option_feedback: Tense and time words must change.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: "Yes, I broke the window," said Raju. → Raju ____ that he had broken the window.
option_feedback: It is a statement, not a question.
Raju is confessing, not giving an order.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: "I'll help you with maths," my brother said to me. → My brother ____ me that he would help me with maths.
option_feedback: An offer of help is a promise, not an order.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: The guide said, "The museum was built in 1890." → The guide said that the museum ____ built in 1890.
questions.explanation: *was built → had been built* (a historical fact may also stay *was built*).
option_feedback: The building happened in the past.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: He said to me, "Are you happy?" → He asked me ____.
Choose the correct reported form: The teacher said to Tina, "Why are you late?" → The teacher asked Tina ____.
Choose the correct reported form: She said to me, "Do you know French?" → She asked me ____ French.
option_feedback: Reported questions lose *do* and the question order.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: He said, "Where did you buy this?" → He asked me where I ____ that.
option_feedback: The backshift of *did buy* is *had bought*.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: "How old are you?" the doctor asked the boy. → The doctor asked the boy ____.
Choose the correct reported form: "Can you lend me a pen?" Arjun asked Meera. → Arjun asked Meera ____ lend him a pen.
Choose the correct reported form: "Who broke this vase?" Mother asked. → Mother asked ____ that vase.
Choose the correct reported form: "Will you come to my party?" said Neha to Pooja. → Neha asked Pooja ____.
options: whether will she come to my party
whether she will come to her party
that she would come to her party
whether she would come to her party

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: "What are you doing here?" the guard said to the boys. → The guard asked the boys what they ____.
Choose the correct reported form: "Have you ever been to Shimla?" my uncle asked me. → My uncle asked me if I ____ to Shimla.
option_feedback: *ever* comes after the helping verb: *had ever been*.
The backshift of *have been* is *had been*.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: The officer said to the soldiers, "Fire!" → The officer ____ the soldiers to fire.
option_feedback: *Fire!* is a command, not a polite request.
It is an order, not advice.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: She said to me, "Please help me." → She ____.
option_feedback: *Please* shows a request, not an order.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: The doctor said to him, "Don't eat junk food." → The doctor advised him ____ junk food.
Choose the correct reported form: "Let's watch a movie," said Kiran. → Kiran ____ watch a movie.
option_feedback: Reported speech must not repeat the exact words.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: The teacher said, "Open your books, children." → The teacher ____ the children to open their books.
option_feedback: *said* cannot take an object like *the children* + *to*.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: "Could you please close the door?" the old man said to me. → The old man ____ the door.
option_feedback: A polite request is reported with *requested/asked + to*.
*Could you please* is polite, not an order.
The pattern is *requested me to close*.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: "Don't swim in the lake," the guard said to us. → The guard ____ swim in the lake.

*Mother: No, you have an exam tomorrow.*

options: if he would like to try it on

questions.question:
Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Coach: Run faster, Meera! Don't stop now.*
*Meera: I am trying my best, sir.*

The coach urged Meera ____.
options: run faster and don't stop now
to run faster and not stop now
to run faster and not to stop then

questions.question:
Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Coach: Run faster, Meera! Don't stop now.*
*Meera: I am trying my best, sir.*

Meera replied respectfully that ____.
questions.explanation: *I am trying my → she was trying her*.

questions.question:
Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Principal: Who painted this beautiful poster?*
*Sana: I did, ma'am. I made it for the science exhibition.*

The principal asked ____.
options: that who had painted that poster
who had painted that beautiful poster
who did paint that beautiful poster
option_feedback: No question mark; *this → that*; *painted → had painted*.

questions.question:
Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Principal: Who painted this beautiful poster?*
*Sana: I did, ma'am. I made it for the science exhibition.*

Sana replied politely that ____ for the science exhibition.
options: she had painted it and had made it
I did and I made it
she did and she makes it
she has painted it and made it
questions.explanation: *I did / I made → she had painted / had made*.

questions.question:
Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Grandfather: Switch off the fan when you leave the room.*
*Kunal: Sorry, Dadaji, I forgot. I will remember next time.*

Grandfather told Kunal ____ the fan when he left the room.
option_feedback: Commands are not reported with *that* + V1.
Grandfather wants the fan switched off.

questions.question:
Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Grandfather: Switch off the fan when you leave the room.*
*Kunal: Sorry, Dadaji, I forgot. I will remember next time.*

Kunal apologised, saying that he ____ and that he ____ the next time.

Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Interviewer: How long have you been playing chess?*
*Gukesh: Since I was seven. I practise for six hours every day.*

The interviewer asked Gukesh how long ____ chess.
questions.explanation: *have you been playing → he had been playing*.
option_feedback: Present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous.
Statement order and pronoun change are needed.

questions.question:
Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Interviewer: How long have you been playing chess?*
*Gukesh: Since I was seven. I practise for six hours every day.*

Gukesh replied that he had been playing since he was seven and that he ____ for six hours every day.
option_feedback: *is* is present; and the habit is reported in the past.
*practise* is the base form; after *replied* it moves back to *practised*.

questions.question:
Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Tourist: Excuse me, is there a good restaurant near here?*
*Policeman: Yes, there is one at the end of this road.*

The tourist politely asked the policeman ____.
options: if there was a good restaurant near there
is there a good restaurant near here
if there is a good restaurant near here
if was there a good restaurant near there

questions.question:
Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Tourist: Excuse me, is there a good restaurant near here?*
*Policeman: Yes, there is one at the end of this road.*

The policeman replied that there was one at the end of ____ road.

Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Sister: Please don't tell Mummy that I broke her cup.*
*Brother: All right, but you must tell her yourself.*

The sister begged her brother ____ that she had broken her cup.
questions.explanation: Negative request → *begged + object + not to + V1*.
option_feedback: Requests are reported with *(not) to* + V1.

questions.question:
Read the dialogue and choose the option that correctly completes the reported version.

*Sister: Please don't tell Mummy that I broke her cup.*
*Brother: All right, but you must tell her yourself.*

The brother agreed, but said that she ____ tell her herself.
option_feedback: *has to* is present; after *said*, *must → had to*.

options: was I going → I was going

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *He told that he was tired.*
Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *Mother told me don't go out in the sun.*
Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *He asked me that whether I could swim.*

options: suggested us to revise → suggested that we should revise
questions.explanation: *suggest* takes *that … should* or V-ing, not object + *to*.
option_feedback: The main problem is *suggested us to*.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *He asked me did I finish the work.*
options: did I finish → whether I had finished

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *The teacher said that water boiled at 100 °C.*
option_feedback: *said* is fine; the truth stays present.

questions.question: Choose the correctly reported sentence. ("Where is the post office?" the tourist asked me.)
options: The tourist asked me where was the post office.
The tourist asked me where the post office is?
The tourist asked me that where the post office was.
The tourist asked me where the post office was.
questions.explanation: wh- + subject + verb, backshift, full stop.

questions.question: Choose the correctly reported sentence. ("Please wait outside," the nurse said to us.)
options: The nurse said us to wait outside.
The nurse requested that wait outside.
The nurse requested us to wait outside.
The nurse requested us please wait outside.

questions.question: Choose the correctly reported sentence. ("I have been working here for ten years," said Mr Rao.)
options: Mr Rao said that I had been working there for ten years.
Mr Rao said that he had been working there for ten years.
Mr Rao said that he has been working there for ten years.
Mr Rao said that he had been working here for ten years.
